notes: C5 treats instruction-fetch metadata as a bus-request record transfer; the primary-asset bars therefore leave its listed output fields without a qualifying primary.
C6 includes bus-request fields only as secondary paths because bus request record fields are barred from being primary.
The RTL implements icc_tx_o as a concurrent constant assignment in the disabled generate branch at line 455, consistent with the diagram's icc_disabled block.

points.reason: The register-file instance stores the architectural contents, exposes selected contents on rs1, rs2 and rs3, and accepts writeback and debug-controlled operations that can disclose, alter, suppress or redirect state.

points.reached by: neorv32_cpu_regfile_inst ==> neorv32_cpu_alu_inst via rs1, rs2 and rs3
points.reason: Register operands reach the ALU and its result can be selected for register writeback, but this internal point has no direct register-state observation or blocking mechanism.
The rs2 register value is used as LSU write data and can therefore leave the unit in dbus_req_o.data.
Control and debug inputs determine register-file operation, including whether writeback occurs and which register operands are selected.

points.reached by: neorv32_cpu_alu_inst ==> rf_wdata via alu_res, and subsequent writeback feedback to the register file
points.reason: rf_wdata is the writeback value accepted by the register-file instance, so corruption or suppression changes or prevents architectural state updates.
The OR-combined writeback value is computed here and sent to the register file, where it can be observed through later architectural reads, corrupted, or withheld.
The ALU result is one operand of the writeback value, so changing it changes the value written to the register file.
Load data is an operand of rf_wdata and can be disclosed through the eventual register writeback or changed before that writeback.

points.reached by: neorv32_cpu_control_inst ==> rf_wdata via csr_rdata and ctrl.pc_ret
points.reason: Control-generated CSR and return-PC values participate in writeback, while the control record can suppress the register-file update.
The register-file instance receives and stores rf_wdata, making the value available to later register reads and allowing writeback corruption or suppression.
The three machine-interrupt inputs are combined into irq_machine, so injected or held request values can alter or indefinitely divert control execution.
The control instance consumes fast and machine interrupt requests to divert execution, and an asserted or repeated request can prevent normal progress.
The unchecked debug request enters control, which produces debug state used by execution units and debug-marked bus accesses, allowing disclosure, modification, parking or bypass of normal execution.
Debug control reaches the frontend that produces the instruction request, and the resulting debug marking is externally visible on ibus_req_o.debug.
Debug control reaches the LSU and its debug-marked data request is visible on dbus_req_o.debug, allowing debug-directed data access behavior.
The frontend instance directly produces the instruction request, whose address, direction and strobe are observable and whose generation can be altered or suppressed.
The ALU produces the effective-address value consumed by the LSU, so changing its result changes the addressed access.
The LSU uses the effective address and direction to generate the externally visible data request, so the access pattern can be observed, changed or suppressed.
The effective address is an input to the protection check, so changing it changes the permission verdict and can permit or block the access.
The calculated address and LSU hand-off affect control's access completion and request behavior, so corruption or blocking can change or prevent the operation.
The frontend consumes the instruction response error and produces frontend.fault, so a forged or suppressed response error changes fault handling or can stop instruction progress.
Control consumes the frontend fault status to decide how instruction execution proceeds, so changing it can accept a failed fetch or hold execution in fault handling.
The LSU consumes the data-response error and produces lsu_err, so a forged or suppressed error changes access completion and recovery.
Control consumes lsu_err to complete or fault the access, so changing it can accept an invalid operation or stall recovery.
The PMP instance produces pmp_fault from the access address, and changing the verdict can permit an unauthorized access or fault every access.
When PMP is disabled, the generate branch forces pmp_fault low, bypassing the protection verdict.
The LSU uses pmp_fault to permit or block data transfers, so the verdict can bypass protection or prevent required accesses.
Control consumes the verdict when handling the access, so corruption can change permission behavior or fault handling.
The LSU produces lsu_wait, and corrupting or holding this status changes whether a pending data operation is allowed to complete.
Control uses lsu_wait to hold or advance execution, so a false value can accept incomplete data or stall indefinitely.
The ALU computes alu_cmp, and changing it changes conditional execution and can direct control onto a non-progressing path.
Control uses the comparison result to select control flow, so a forged result can execute the wrong path or prevent forward progress.
The ALU produces alu_cp_done, and forging or suppressing it can retire an incomplete operation or keep control waiting.
Control uses the completion hand-off to retire or continue the coprocessor operation, so corruption changes retirement and suppression can stall it.
The ALU status source contributes to xcsr_res, so changing it changes the CSR read-back value.
The counter read-data source contributes to xcsr_res, so changing it changes the CSR read-back value.
The PMP CSR source contributes to xcsr_res, so changing it changes protection-related read-back data.
The ICC CSR source contributes to xcsr_res, so changing it changes the read-back word.
xcsr_res merges the status sources and passes the merged word into control for CSR read-back, so it can disclose or corrupt returned status.
The control instance consumes xcsr_res and produces csr_rdata, which is selected for software-visible register writeback and can therefore disclose or falsify status.
csr_rdata is mixed into rf_wdata before register writeback, so the read-back word can be disclosed or changed at this computation.
The read-back value is written into the register file and can subsequently be observed as architectural state or corrupted before storage.
